newsitem.title: INDIA: FOCUS-BJP seen taking lead in Uttar Pradesh polls.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BJP seen taking lead in Uttar Pradesh polls.

text.p: India's main opposition, the Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), was leading in elections for the country's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh, officials said on Wednesday.
They said results in 10 state seats had been declared so far with the BJP winning seven, the Congress-BSP alliance taking two and the other going to the United Front.
Initial counting indicated the BJP was ahead in 120 out of 281 state seats in the 425-seat assembly, they added.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party United Front alliance led in 79 seats with an alliance of the Congress Party and low-caste Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) ahead in 74.
Smaller parties and independent candidates were leading eight others, officials said.
Any party or coalition will have to win at least 213 seats to stake a claim to forming the next Uttar Pradesh government.
Opinion polls conducted before the elections have forecast a hung assembly for the state.
Election Commission officials in the state capital of Lucknow said most results will be declared by early Friday.
